chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Walid reported to me from his father, who reported from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qashani, from al-Isfahani, from Sulaiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who reported that Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, said:

"When any of you wishes that he does not ask God for anything except that He grants it, then let him despair of all people, and let him have no hope except from God, the Mighty and Majestic. When God knows that from his heart, he will not ask for anything except that He grants it."
So take account of yourselves before you are called to account, for on the Day of Resurrection there will be fifty stations, each station equal to a thousand years of what you reckon.
Then he recited this verse: 'In a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years.'

key_terms.رجاء: Hope, expectation — a spiritual state of placing one's trust and expectations
key_terms.فحاسبوا أنفسكم: Take account of yourselves — a well-known ethical maxim urging self-examination before the Divine reckoning
key_terms.موقف: Station — one of the stages or standing places on the Day of Judgment

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about relying on God alone for having prayers answered?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that the key to having one's prayers answered is to place complete reliance on God alone and abandon all hope in people. He was addressing his companions, reminding them that self-accounting in this world is crucial because the Day of Resurrection contains fifty stations, each lasting a thousand years. He concluded by citing Quran 70:4 to emphasize the immense duration of that Day.
